Robot Doctor Servos

Servo doesn't reach full range or the right angle

Moves less than advertised or ends up in the wrong place. Below are the 4 most common causes on FTC robots, ordered from most to least likely, with how to check and fix each one.

Skip the guesswork — run the interactive diagnosisAbout 4 quick questions narrow this list down to your robot's actual problem.

Quick checks first

  • Does it move the right amount but in the wrong spot (shifted)? The total swing is fine, it is just not lined up with the mechanism.
  • Have you widened the PWM range (setPwmRange) or programmed the servo's range? By default the SDK uses 600–2400 µs.
  • Is it supposed to spin continuously (like an intake roller)? Continuous servos spin; position servos go to an angle.
  • Does it buzz or jitter only at one end of its travel? Move it to each end position and listen.

Common causes and how to fix them

1 Default PWM range limits travel

The SDK maps 0–1 to 600–2400 µs by default, so many servos (goBILDA, REV Smart Robot Servo) show less range than advertised.

How to fix it 5 min

  1. Widen the range with setPwmRange (up to 500–2500 µs). Then 0 and 1 cover the full travel.
  2. Check your servo's spec sheet for its real pulse range before going wider.
  3. Programmable servos (Axon, SRS) can also have their own range set with the programmer.
Widen the PWM range
ServoImplEx claw = hardwareMap.get(ServoImplEx.class, "claw");
claw.setPwmRange(new PwmControl.PwmRange(500, 2500));

Sources: GM0 · How the SDK drives servos · GM0 · Servo usage tips

2 Horn or linkage mounted at the wrong angle

The servo is fine, but its range is not centered on the motion you need.

How to fix it 10 min

  1. Command 0.5, then mount the horn or arm at the middle of the motion you want.
  2. Then find your real endpoints with telemetry and a gamepad nudge.

Sources: GM0 · Servo usage tips

3 Servo configured as the wrong type or mode

A continuous servo set up as a regular Servo (or the reverse) does not behave, and some servos have their own modes.

How to fix it 5 min

  1. In the configuration, pick "Servo" for position servos and "Continuous Rotation Servo" for spinning ones.
  2. goBILDA dual-mode and Axon servos can be switched between position and continuous with their programmer. Make sure the servo is in the mode your code expects.
  3. Continuous servos use setPower (CRServo). Position servos use setPosition between 0 and 1.

Sources: GM0 · Servo usage tips · GM0 · How the SDK drives servos

4 Servo pushing against a hard stop

If the commanded position is past where the mechanism physically stops, the servo strains, buzzes, gets hot, and draws lots of current.

How to fix it 10 min

  1. Command the position slowly in small steps and find where the mechanism actually stops. Keep the endpoints just short of it.
  2. Re-index the horn or linkage so the full range fits the mechanism.

Sources: GM0 · Servo usage tips
